summary: Heath Black introduces himself and SignalFire, a VC firm built like a tech company that interviewed 500 founders to build AI/ML tools around their problems. SignalFire's proprietary Beacon platform tracks 650 million employees, 80 million companies, and 200 million open-source projects to power ranking systems and market insights for portfolio companies. The talk covers four areas: filters, location, timing, and narrative. On filters, Black highlights a stark de-credentialization in AI: in 2015, 27% of engineer hires came from top schools and 16% had PhDs; by 2023 those fell to 15% and 7%, roughly 50% declines. He attributes this to a market shift from foundational ML research to applied ML/Ops and product experience. Talent has concentrated in nine "AI League" companies, with big tech fighting to pull talent from them. On location, San Francisco dominates with 35% of all AI engineers, followed by Seattle at 22% and New York at 10%, with SF capturing 38% of early-stage AI funding. On timing, Black discusses retention rates (Anthropic ~66% vs. Perplexity ~43%), generational behavior (Gen Z job-hopping at 2.2 jobs in four years vs. Gen X's 1.1), and SignalFire's historical composition tool that snapshots admired companies' org structures at different stages. On narrative, Black draws on Kurt Vonnegut's shape-of-stories concept, using the Cinderella arc as metaphor for company storytelling—understanding where you've been, where you are, and where your arc is going. He warns that salary and equity alone no longer suffice: from November 2022 to November 2024, average tech salaries rose only 1.6%, equity grants declined precipitously, and AI engineers command 5% salary and 10-20% equity premiums over other engineering roles. Share exercising fell to 33% in Q2 2024 from 55% a couple years prior, driven by valuation concerns and market volatility. Black argues companies must craft narratives around non-monetary factors: close-knit teams, founder access, collaborative culture, speed, lack of friction, big mission, career growth, exploding markets, and complex problems. He closes by advising job seekers to track where admired people go, how long they stay, and what they want in their career arc.

sections.title: Introduction and SignalFire Overview
sections.summary: Heath Black introduces his background from Irish literature to startups (Chirpify, Imzy, Reddit, Meta) and his current role at SignalFire, a VC firm built like a tech company that interviewed 500 founders to build AI/ML tools around their problems. He introduces the Beacon platform tracking 650M employees, 80M companies, and 200M open-source projects.

sections.title: Filters: De-credentialization and Talent Mobility
sections.summary: Covers the decline in PhD and top-school requirements for AI engineers (~50% drop from 2015 to 2023), the shift toward applied ML experience over research credentials, talent concentration in nine AI League companies, and net employee movement data between companies. Recommends removing academic requirements and focusing on body of work.

sections.title: Location: Where AI Talent Concentrates
sections.summary: Analyzes geographic distribution of AI talent. San Francisco leads with 35% of AI engineers, followed by Seattle (22%) and New York (10%). SF also captures 38% of early-stage AI funding. Emphasizes that data, not Twitter debates, determines market viability and that location still matters in a distributed world.

sections.title: Timing: Retention, Generations, and Historical Composition
sections.summary: Explores timing in recruiting through retention rates (Anthropic ~66% vs. Perplexity ~43%), generational job-hopping (Gen Z 27% turnover in 2023, 2.2 jobs in four years vs. Gen X 1.1), and SignalFire's historical composition tool for identifying risk profiles and 10x hires at the right company stage.

sections.title: Narrative: Shaping Your Company Story
sections.summary: Introduces narrative as the fourth pillar, drawing on Vonnegut's shape-of-stories concept and the Cinderella arc as metaphor for company storytelling. Warns that salary and equity alone no longer suffice: tech salaries rose only 1.6% from Nov 2022 to Nov 2024, AI engineers command 5% salary and 10-20% equity premiums, and share exercising fell to 33% in Q2 2024 from 55% previously. Companies must build narratives around non-monetary factors—founder access, collaborative teams, speed, mission, career growth, exploding markets, and complex problems. Closes with advice for job seekers to track where admired people go, how long they stay, and to understand their own career arc.
